title: Stroke: history or residual deficits
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's past stroke and any residual deficits.
note:
Chief Complaint: Evaluation of residual left-sided hemiparesis.

HPI: The patient is a 68-year-old man who presents today for a follow-up evaluation of his chronic mobility and motor function. He has a history of a previous ischemic stroke that resulted in residual left-sided hemiparesis. He notes that while he has adapted to his condition, he continues to experience some difficulty with fine motor tasks. He notes that he is left-handed, which complicates his daily activities due to the motor limitations on his left side. He denies any recent falls or sudden changes in his strength.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40mg daily
- Aspirin 81mg daily

Exam: The patient is alert and oriented. Vital signs are stable. Physical examination reveals persistent left-sided hemiparesis. Strength is diminished in the left upper and lower extremities. He is notably left-hand dominant, and his grip strength is significantly lower on the left side compared to the right.

Assessment: 
1. Residual left-sided hemiparesis following a prior ischemic stroke.

Plan:
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Refer to physical therapy to work on gait stability and strengthening.
3. Follow up in three months.

Electronically signed,
K. Nguyen, PA-C
05/14/2026
explanations: Residual hemiparesis after an ischemic stroke, left dominant side: I69.352 (HCC 253).

distractors.why: Check the documented handedness; when it is not documented, the right side is dominant and the left side non-dominant.
Residual hemiparesis is documented: code the sequela (I69.35-, HCC 253), not Z86.73.
